questions.question: [MCQ] The primary purpose of subsurface (tile) drainage in agricultural land is to:

options.B: lower the water table and remove excess soil water from the root zone
options.C: increase soil salinity in the root zone
options.D: improve the uniformity of surface irrigation application

questions.solution:

Q.54 Solution:• Correct Answer: 80.0 to 88.0• Section: Agricultural Engineering | Sub-topic: Soil and Water Erosion | Type: NAT | Marks: 2Q.54   [Soil & Water Conservation Engineering → Soil and Water Erosion]   [NAT, 2 marks]Question: Runoff from a 2-hectare plot during a storm carries away soil equivalent to a uniform erosion depth of 3 mm over the entire plot. If the bulk density of the eroded soil is 1400 kg/m³, the total mass of soil eroded (in tonnes) is ______ (round off to one decimal place).Answer: 80.0 to 88.0Explanation: Volume of soil eroded = Plot area × erosion depth = (2 × 10,000 m²) × 0.003 m = 60 m³.Mass eroded = Volume × bulk density = 60 m³ × 1400 kg/m³ = 84,000 kg = 84.0 t.

questions.question: [MSQ] For particulate agricultural materials handled by conveyors, which of the following statement(s) is/are correct?

options.A: The capacity of a belt conveyor increases with belt speed, for a given belt width and material cross-section
options.B: The angle of surcharge of a material is always greater than its angle of repose
options.C: The maximum permissible incline angle of a belt conveyor decreases as the material becomes more free-flowing
options.D: Screw conveyors are generally preferred over belt conveyors for vertical or steeply inclined transport of grain

questions.solution:
Q.60 Solution:• Correct Answer: A, C, D• Section: Agricultural Engineering | Sub-topic: Size Reduction and Material Handling | Type: MSQ | Marks: 2Q.60   [Agricultural Process Engineering → Size Reduction and Material Handling]   [MSQ, 2 marks]Question: For particulate agricultural materials handled by conveyors, which of the following statement(s) is/are correct?(A) The capacity of a belt conveyor increases with belt speed, for a given belt width and material cross-section   (B) The angle of surcharge of a material is always greater than its angle of repose   (C) The maximum permissible incline angle of a belt conveyor decreases as the material becomes more free-flowing   (D) Screw conveyors are generally preferred over belt conveyors for vertical or steeply inclined transport of grainAnswer: A, C, DExplanation: (A) is correct: conveyor capacity = (belt speed) × (cross-sectional area of the material load), so capacity scales directly with speed for a fixed area.(C) is correct: free-flowing materials (low angle of repose) slide back readily, so the permissible incline for a belt conveyor is lower for such materials.(D) is correct: screw conveyors can convey material vertically or at steep inclines, which belt conveyors handle poorly.(B) is incorrect: the angle of surcharge (the dynamic angle the material forms on a moving belt) is generally less than or equal to the (static) angle of repose, not always greater.

questions.question: [MSQ] For heat transfer during milk pasteurization in a plate heat exchanger operating in counter-current flow, which of the following statement(s) is/are correct?

options.A: The log mean temperature difference (LMTD) for counter-current flow is greater than or equal to that for co-current (parallel) flow, for the same inlet/outlet temperatures
options.B: Counter-current flow can achieve an outlet temperature of the cold fluid higher than the outlet temperature of the hot fluid
options.C: The overall heat transfer coefficient depends only on the fluid properties and not on flow velocity, geometry, or plate fouling
options.D: Fouling of the heat exchanger plates decreases the overall heat transfer coefficient over time

questions.solution:
Q.63 Solution:• Correct Answer: A, B, D• Section: Agricultural Engineering | Sub-topic: Heat and Mass Transfer | Type: MSQ | Marks: 2Q.63   [Dairy & Food Engineering → Heat and Mass Transfer]   [MSQ, 2 marks]Question: For heat transfer during milk pasteurization in a plate heat exchanger operating in counter-current flow, which of the following statement(s) is/are correct?(A) The log mean temperature difference (LMTD) for counter-current flow is greater than or equal to that for co-current (parallel) flow, for the same inlet/outlet temperatures   (B) Counter-current flow can achieve an outlet temperature of the cold fluid higher than the outlet temperature of the hot fluid   (C) The overall heat transfer coefficient depends only on the fluid properties and not on flow velocity, geometry, or plate fouling   (D) Fouling of the heat exchanger plates decreases the overall heat transfer coefficient over timeAnswer: A, B, DExplanation: (A) is correct: for identical terminal temperatures, counter-current LMTD ≥ co-current LMTD, which is why counter-current configurations achieve the required duty with less heat transfer area.(B) is correct: this 'temperature cross' is a distinguishing capability of counter-current arrangements, not possible in co-current flow.(D) is correct: fouling adds thermal resistance in series, reducing the overall coefficient with time.(C) is incorrect: the overall coefficient depends on both film coefficients (which depend on velocity and geometry) and the fouling resistance, not on fluid properties alone.

questions.question: [MSQ] In the context of moisture transfer during the drying of a food material, which of the following statement(s) is/are correct?

options.A: Mass transfer by diffusion follows Fick's law, analogous to heat conduction following Fourier's law
options.B: The convective mass transfer coefficient generally increases with increasing air velocity over the product surface
options.C: During the falling rate period, internal moisture diffusion within the solid is typically the rate-limiting step
options.D: The equilibrium moisture content of a hygroscopic material is independent of the relative humidity of the surrounding air

questions.solution:
Q.64 Solution:• Correct Answer: A, B, C• Section: Agricultural Engineering | Sub-topic: Heat and Mass Transfer | Type: MSQ | Marks: 2Q.64   [Dairy & Food Engineering → Heat and Mass Transfer]   [MSQ, 2 marks]Question: In the context of moisture transfer during the drying of a food material, which of the following statement(s) is/are correct?(A) Mass transfer by diffusion follows Fick's law, analogous to heat conduction following Fourier's law   (B) The convective mass transfer coefficient generally increases with increasing air velocity over the product surface   (C) During the falling rate period, internal moisture diffusion within the solid is typically the rate-limiting step   (D) The equilibrium moisture content of a hygroscopic material is independent of the relative humidity of the surrounding airAnswer: A, B, CExplanation: (A) is correct: Fick's first law (mass flux ∝ concentration gradient) is mathematically analogous to Fourier's law (heat flux ∝ temperature gradient).(B) is correct: higher air velocity thins the boundary layer at the product surface, increasing the convective mass transfer coefficient.(C) is correct: once the surface can no longer supply moisture as fast as it evaporates, internal diffusion through the solid controls the drying rate.(D) is incorrect: equilibrium moisture content is strongly dependent on the surrounding relative humidity (and temperature), as described by sorption isotherms.
